### The
### PREFACE to the Reader of
# Jacob Boehme's
## Book of Christ’s Incarnation.

***Reader,***

It is a prominent text: *“Search the Scriptures, for in them you think you have eternal life; and they are they which testify of ME. And you will not come to ME that you might have life,”* John 5:39–40. These are the words of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ to the Jews at Jerusalem during the days of his time <note>original: "Conversation"; here referring to his life, conduct, and social presence among humanity</note> on earth in mortal *flesh*. They thought they had eternal life in the Scriptures and were physically present with Christ, yet they would not come to him, even though the Scriptures are what testify of him. By this, it may appear that coming to Christ must necessarily be *inward*, by coming to be like him in their hearts and becoming meek and lowly of heart. Such people only, and no others, *come* to him in any age or place of this world or in eternity; nor can any others possibly have life.

Though the Holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testament are indeed the written word of God, written by the holy prophets and apo-

Yet if we consider it seriously, can we think that the eternal, ever-living Word—CHRIST JESUS—by whom all things were created, and who is God himself, has spoken through his Word in all his holy ones? These holy ones spoke the *things* mentioned in the Scriptures, which were recorded there by the command of that *same Word*. 

I say, when we weigh this, can we really believe that this powerful Word (which is God) would want *only* the Scriptures to be *called* the "Word of God"? Should the living power be dismissed as *unobserved*? Or should those texts that speak of the Word be interpreted as referring only to the Holy Scriptures, as if no such thing existed besides them? In reality, the Scriptures were written for the sake of *that* Word; holy men spoke, and God has performed all things by and for *it*, for his own glory.

Furthermore, should the writing be *preferred* over the subject written about? That subject—the Word—is what caused and dictated the writing. Yet some people think that the Word *is not* that which fills all things, calling out in the hearts of everyone, even though it is often ignored.

Additionally, the Holy Scripture says that the Word is in the heart. Yet some people do *not* *understand* <note>original: "conceived"</note> it to be there before the Word was known to be written by any man, or spoken by a human

whoever finds him, can he *miss* finding *ALL THINGS*? It seems strange that this idea should enter into the heart of any man; and yet, we are so tied up by previous perceptions <note>original: "apprehensions"</note> and conclusions fixed in our minds that further consideration of it cannot easily take place or sink into us. This may make us pause for a while and examine what the *cause* of this might be.

And then we may observe that our *disposition* is commonly such that we do not love to hear opposition or a different perspective from others, lest we should be led to think and believe something contrary to our previously *framed basis of opinion*, which was *abstracted* from outward senses alone. This is because when that basis is once removed, all conclusions built upon it fall to the ground. Thus we lose all that great labor and are forced to work anew upon a new foundation. Then there is a fear that if this new foundation should be shaken again, there must be another labor with the same *risk of unprofitable success*. 

This is such a massive discouragement to any mind that it eventually becomes *languishing* and, as it were, dead—especially if an assured, infallible, and immovable internal ground is not presented to it, so that it may go on cheerfully to build, hoping to enjoy the fruit of beholding the *beauty* of its *superstructure* <note>The "superstructure" refers to the complex system of beliefs or knowledge built upon a foundational principle.</note>. And when the mind is thus "dead" to its own efforts, it is most capable of being taught by the quickening <note>original: "quickening," meaning life-giving or awakening</note> Spirit of Truth that lies hidden within it, beneath its former but merely supposed truths.

Yet, to deny that the Holy Scriptures are the written word of God—or the Word of God expressed in writing—is not only to oppose *obvious* <note>original: "apparent"</note> truth, but also to undervalue that precious help for knowing and understanding what *that Word* <note>The author refers to the "Inward Word" or Holy Spirit that inspired the biblical authors.</note> was that inspired the writing in the first place. This is the very purpose <note>original: "End"</note> for which the Word was written down and preserved for us. It is one of the most excellent fruits of the wisdom found in literature <note>original: "Letters"</note> which that Eternal Word has produced in this outward, visible, and temporary <note>original: "transitory"</note> world.

However, valuing that "fruit" and looking after it *more* than the "Root," and setting it up instead of—and *above*—the hidden Word in all things, is a temptation placed in human hearts by the suggestion of the Great Enemy <note>original: "Arch-Enemy," referring to the Devil.</note> of all mankind. He knows well enough that if the inward Word is once *choked* and *killed* at the root, so that it is no longer felt, known, and obeyed, he will soon cause evil minds to use that *most precious literal Word* merely as a pretext to cover all sin with hypocrisy. This causes the Word in the heart to be completely ignored or forgotten. 

On the contrary, whoever deeply values the Word—the Commandment, Christ in the heart, and 그hat word of faith from which the heart itself originally draws its very *existence*—cannot fail to value its powerful work. This is the inexpressibly *diverse* wisdom that dwells in the heart and appears through the mouth or pen of any person whatsoever.

# The Preface.

Therefore, read <note>original: "peruse"</note> this book, which will inform us how the Eternal Word became human and how the man *JESUS CHRIST*—who was born of the *Virgin Mary* and lived upon Earth for more than thirty-three years—was then crucified, died, was buried, rose again, and ascended into Heaven. This took place within a *small part* of the world: the regions of *Egypt*, the *Wilderness*, the land of *Canaan*, *Judea*, and the city of *Jerusalem*, in the fullness of time, about 1,658 years ago. 

*How HE* was also this Eternal Word, which was, is, and ever shall be: God and Christ, the eternal *Alpha* and *Omega* <note>The first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, symbolizing the beginning and the end.</note>, the beginning and the end, and the word of Faith. He is that very Word which is in our hearts—the Word of Life, the implanted <note>original: "inserted or ingrafted"</note> Word, the Word of Grace, the Spirit of Life, and the Bread which came down from Heaven and which *always is* in Heaven. This is not the physical <note>original: "outward"</note> bread, though it is present within the physical bread; for we do not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God. This is the Bread of Life, our

# The Preface.

...laid open in this book. Once these truths are understood, they may eventually bring us to a full understanding of everything the Scriptures contain—except for what the Spirit of God chooses to conceal. An example of this is what the *seven thunders* <note>A reference to Revelation 10:3–4, where John is told to seal up what the seven thunders uttered and not write it down.</note> in the *Book of Revelation* <note>original: "Revelations"</note> sounded forth. Yet, those things that the Spirit will *not yet* reveal—which the Father reserves in His own power until the time for their accomplishment is near—will still be made known to the soul. Even so, such things might be understood by one holy soul or another *according to the nature of the thing* <term>nature of the thing</term> <note>Understanding the essential character or reality of a spiritual truth through direct insight before it is publicly revealed to all.</note>, with a command not to make it known to others.

Yet, even if we understand things ever so perfectly in our spirits, souls, and heavenly bodies within our *inward man* <term>inward man</term> <note>The spiritual or internal self, as described by St. Paul, in contrast to the physical, "outward" body.</note>, we enjoy them only inwardly in assured hope. We do not yet see them as we shall, nor do we enjoy them as we will when we experience them just as we now experience this world with our *outward body*. *Both* of these will be changed together at the end. And although this body <margin>1 Corinthians 15:42–43</margin> is *sown in weakness, at its resurrection, it is raised in power as a spiritual, incorruptible, immortal, and eternal body, made to conform to Christ’s glorious body* for those who have partaken of Him in this life.

This will take place in that world where all evil will be done away with. First, it will be removed from sticking and adhering to us, as it does now in and through our *outward man* in this life. Then, also, all corruption will be eliminated at the transformation <note>original: "change"</note> of this world and the resurrection of the body. # The Preface.

...eternal bliss; *then corruption shall put on incorruption* <note>original: "Corruption shall put on Incorruption"; a reference to 1 Corinthians 15:53—the transformation of the mortal body into an immortal one.</note>, *and God shall be all in all*; yet all things will remain what they then are, though God will be present in every one of them.

In the meantime, we may attain perfection in our souls, spirits, and new heavenly bodies, being truly members of Christ within us. Yet we should subdue our bodies daily and *mortify* <term>mortify</term> <note>To subdue or "kill off" physical desires or sins through spiritual discipline.</note> our physical parts <note>original: "Members that are on the Earth"; referring to worldly desires or sins as parts of the physical body.</note>. We must learn how every one of us may justly consider ourselves the very chief of sinners, finding sin to be exceedingly sinful. Through this, we should strive through *godly sorrow* to produce a holy *indignation* within us against sin. We must learn how sin dwells in us, even though we should *not* let it reign in our mortal bodies or obey its lusts. If, by the Spirit, we thus mortify the deeds of the body, we shall live; for then we bring forth the fruits of the Spirit, *in which we are perfect even in this life*.

Because this treatise will so greatly help us in these various *divine* considerations, I ask the reader, for their own benefit, to read it seriously. They will find, as I have, more than they can currently imagine before reading it—even though I, viewing myself in the looking-glass <term>looking-glass</term> <note>A mirror. Here, Sparrow uses the metaphor of a mirror to describe self-reflection and the recognition of one's own sins.</note> of my sins, find <margin>my</margin> just cause to acknowledge myself as one of the unworthiest of the children of men.

1. When Christ asked his disciples, *“Who do the people say that the Son of Man is?”* They answered, “Some say you are Elijah, some that you are John the Baptist, or one of the Prophets.”

2. He asked them, “But who do you say that I am?”

3. Then Peter answered him, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

4. And he answered them and said, “In truth, flesh and blood has not revealed that to you, but my Father in Heaven;” and upon this, he made known to them his suffering, death, and resurrection.

5. This was to signify that "self-reason" <term>self-reason</term> <note>original: "self Reason"; Boehme uses this to describe human logic or intellect operating independently of divine revelation.</note>, within the intelligence and wisdom of this world, could not by its own logic know or comprehend this Person, who was both God and man.

6. Instead, he would, for the most part, be rightly known only by those who would wholly yield themselves up to him, and for his name’s sake endure the Cross, tribulation, and persecution—those who would earnestly cling to him.

7. As indeed it also happened then: even while he lived visibly among us in this world, he was least known by those who were "wise" in their own human reason.

8. And though he went up and down performing divine wonders and doing miracles, outward reason was so blind and void of understanding that those great wonders were attributed to the Devil by those most learned in the arts and sciences of human logic.

<summary>This page introduces the central theme of the book: that the Incarnation of Christ cannot be understood through human reason alone, but only through spiritual surrender and divine revelation. It uses the Gospel of Matthew to illustrate how the "wise" of the world failed to recognize Christ despite his miracles.</summary>
<keywords>Incarnation, Jesus Christ, Self-Reason, Divine Revelation, Matthew 16, Miracles, Eternal Principles, Jacob Boehme</keywords>

--- Page 31 ---
<meta>This page continues Chapter 1 of Part I. On the previous page, the author introduced the concept that human reason ("self-reason") is unable to comprehend the dual nature of Christ as both God and man, noting that only those who yield to the Spirit can truly know him.</meta>

9. Just as he remained unknown to those who were "wise" in their own logic when he walked visibly in this world, he still remains unknown to *external human reason*.

10. Because of this, so much argument, debate, and conflict have arisen regarding his Person. External reason assumes it can reach, fathom, and investigate what God and man are, and how God and man can be one Person.

11. This conflict has filled the entire Earth. Human logic continually assumes it has found and obtained the "Pearl" <note>original: "the Pearl"; a reference to the "pearl of great price" from Matthew 13:46, symbolizing spiritual truth or Christ himself.</note>, without considering that God’s Kingdom is *not* of this world, and that "flesh and blood" <note>original: "Flesh and Blood"; refers to human nature in its fallen or purely physical state, which cannot perceive spiritual reality.</note> cannot know or grasp it.

12. Therefore, it is now vital for everyone who wishes to speak or teach about the Divine Mysteries to possess the Spirit of God. They must understand the truths they present in the Light of God, rather than drawing them from their own logic. Otherwise, *without* divine knowledge, they follow the "bare letter" <term>bare letter</term> <note>original: "bare Letter"; refers to a literal or academic reading of scripture without spiritual insight.</note> of their own opinions and "drag the Scripture by the hair" <note>original: "drag the Scripture by the Hair of the Head"; a colorful idiom meaning to force or twist the meaning of the Bible to fit one's own agenda.</note> to prove their points, as is *usually* done by human reason.

13. Countless errors have arisen from this because divine knowledge has been sought through human cleverness and skill. Consequently, people are pulled away from God's truth toward their own logic, leading them to view the "Becoming-human" or Incarnation of Christ as something *strange* and foreign.

14. Yet we must all be born again of God through that very "Becoming-human" or Incarnation if we are ever to escape the wrath of eternal torment or "Nature" <note>original: "Nature"; in Boehme's thought, this refers to the restless, harsh forces of existence when they are not tempered by God's light.</note>.

15. However, since this is a familiar, intimate, and natural work for the children of God, they should practice it daily and hourly. They should always enter into the "Becoming-human" or Incarnation of Christ and move beyond earthly reason. In this miserable life, they must be born into the birth and Incarnation of Christ if they *intend* to be God’s children in Christ.

<margin>God with us</margin>
16. I have therefore undertaken to write about this profound mystery according to my knowledge and gifts as a memorial. In doing so, I may also have cause to be heartily refreshed and brought to life by my *Immanuel* <note>original: "Immanuel"; Hebrew for "God with us."</note>.

17. Since I, along with the other children of God and Christ, take my stand in this spiritual birth, I write so that I may have a reminder and a support. This is for those times when the dark, earthly "flesh and blood," combined with the Devil’s poison, might surprise me, overcome me, or obscure and darken my inner image.

18. Therefore, I have undertaken this as an exercise of *faith*, through which my soul—like a branch or twig on its tree, *Jesus Christ*—may bring itself to life using his sap and power.

19. This is not done with the clever or high eloquence of academic skill, nor from the logic of this world, but according to the knowledge I have from my tree, *Christ*. My goal is that my little sprout in the tree and life of God may grow and flourish along with others.

<summary>Boehme argues that the Incarnation remains a mystery to human reason and is only accessible through spiritual rebirth and the Holy Spirit. He explains that his writing serves as a personal spiritual exercise to keep his faith rooted in Christ despite the distractions of the physical world.</summary>

# 1. Chapter: Of the Two Eternal Principles, etc. Part I.

I say this out of goodwill and give it to the reader to ponder.

When we write about the Incarnation <note>original: "Becoming Man"</note> and birth of JESUS CHRIST, the Son of God, and speak rightly of it, we must consider the cause. What is it that moved God to become man, seeing that he did not need to do so for the accomplishment or perfection of his own being or substance?

23. Neither can we say by any means that his own being or substance altered itself in the Incarnation.

<margin>God is unchangeable, yet he has become what he was not.</margin>
24. For God is unchangeable, and yet has become what he was not, though his essence remains unaltered for all that. His only aim was the salvation of fallen man, so that he might bring him into Paradise again.

25. And here we are to consider the first man—how he was before his fall—for whose sake the Deity has moved itself. This is something that we humans ought to consider deeply.

<margin>* Genesis 1:26, 27; 5:1; 9:6</margin>

Understand it this way: that God, who is a Spirit, beheld himself in an image, as if in a reflection.

27. Nevertheless, he has also created *this world* so that he might manifest the Eternal Nature in physical substance, and also in living creatures and forms. All this is meant to be a reflection and an *out-birth* <note>original: "out-birth"; an external manifestation or product of a deeper internal reality.</note> or express image of the Eternal Nature of the First Principle <term>First Principle</term> <note>original: "First Principle"; refers to the foundational ground of existence, often associated with the "fire" or power of God the Father in Böhme's system.</note>.

<margin>* or Desire.</margin>
28. Which reflection, before the time of the world, stood in the wisdom of God as a hidden *Magia* <note>original: "Magia"; the creative, working desire or spiritual power that brings things into being; not "magic" in a modern sense.</note>, and was beheld in that wisdom by the Spirit of God.

29. At the beginning of this world, the Spirit moved the Eternal Nature and brought forth the reflection of the hidden divine world.

30. For the *Fiery World* <term>Fiery World</term> <note>original: "Fiery world"; the spiritual realm of energy and strength which, in Böhme’s view, is the underlying source of life, usually hidden by the light of God.</note> stood, as it were, swallowed up or hidden in the light of God, because the light of his Majesty ruled alone within it.

# into its own Principle, and was not manifested in the Light of God's Majesty.

32. As we may observe in *Fire* and *Light*: the Fire is indeed a cause of the Light, and yet the Light dwells in the Fire without being apprehended by the Fire, and it possesses a different source or quality than the Fire.

33. For fire is fierceness and it consumes, whereas light is meekness. Out of the light's virtue or power comes *Substantiality*—namely, "Water," or the *Sulphur* <note>In Böhme’s mystical chemistry, "Sulphur" refers to the combustible, energetic quality of a substance that allows light to manifest.</note> of a thing—which the Fire attracts into itself and uses for its strength and life; thus, it is an eternal bond.

34. This Fire and divine Light have each stood still in themselves from eternity. Each stands in its own order, within its own Principle, having neither ground nor beginning.

<margin>How the Fire's form and Desire arise.</margin>
35. For the Fire has within itself, as its source or quality, its own Form: namely, *Desire*. Out of this Desire, and within it, all forms of Nature are generated—each one being a continual cause of the other, as is explained at length in other writings.

36. And we find in the "Light of Nature" <note>This refers to human reason and the observation of the natural world as a reflection of divine truths.</note> that the Fire, in its own essence, existed as an astringent, desiring source or quality—a *darkness* in itself. In the meekness of God, this darkness stood as if swallowed up, so that it was not active or producing its specific quality, but existed essentially in itself, *and was not kindled*.

37. And though it "burned," as it were, it did so only as its *own* Principle, perceptible *only* within itself.

38. For there have been only *two* Principles from eternity: one in itself, the *Fiery world*; the other also in itself, the *Light-flaming world*.

39. Yet they were not parted from one another, just as fire and light are not parted. The Light dwells in the Fire, unapprehended by the Fire.

40. Thus we are to understand *two Spirits* within one another:
    *   1. One fiery, according to the essence of the astringent and stern nature—arising from the hot and cold sternness of the Essential Fire. This is understood to be God's wrath-spirit, source, or quality, and it belongs to the Father’s property. Because of this, he calls himself a *jealous God* <margin>† Exodus 20:4 <note>original: "Exod. 20. 4." - God describes himself as a jealous God who punishes the iniquity of those who hate him.</note></margin> and *a consuming fire* <margin>* Hebrews 12:29 <note>original: "Heb. 12. 29." - The verse states: "For our God is a consuming fire."</note></margin>, in which the first Principle is understood.

41. And 2. the other a *meek Light-flaming Spirit*, which from eternity undergoes its variation or transformation in the Center of the Light. In the first Principle (the Father's property), it is a Fiery Spirit; in the second Principle (the light), it is a meek, light-flaming spirit. It is only one spirit, not two; but it is understood to exist in *two* sources or qualities—namely, Fire and Light—according to the property of each.

42. This is easily understood by looking at any outward fire, where...

# Chapter 1: Of the Temporary. Part 1.

...in the fire-source <note>The author uses "source" or "quality" to translate the German *Qual*, which implies both a characteristic and a driving, sometimes painful, urge.</note> or quality, it gives a wrathful, fierce spirit that is *consuming*; and the source or quality of the light gives a meek, amiable *Air-Spirit*, and yet it is originally but one Spirit.

43. In like manner, we are to conceive of the Being or Substance of Eternity—namely, the holy *Trinity*—which we understand to be the *Deity* in the Light, and the *Eternal Nature* in the Fire, as is sufficiently cleared in other writings.

44. For the Omnipotent Spirit of God, with both these Principles, has been *everything* itself from eternity; there is nothing before it. It is itself the Ground or *Byss* <note>original: "Byffe". In Böhme’s philosophy, the "Byss" is the grounded foundation of existence, contrasted with the "Abyss."</note> and the *Abyss*.

45. And yet the Holy Divine Being or Substance is especially observed to be a Being or Substance of its own, in itself, and it dwells without or beyond the fiery or firing nature and property, residing in the light’s property; it is called \* GOD, not from the fire's property, but from the light's property.

<margin>\* GOD <note>original: "GOTT"</note>
How fire is in all things</margin>

46. Though indeed *both* properties are unsevered, as we may understand by this world, wherein there lies a hidden Fire in the deep of Nature and hidden in all beings, substances, and things; otherwise, no outward fire could be brought forth.

47. And we see that the meekness of the water holds that hidden fire captive in itself, so that it cannot manifest itself; for it is, as it were, swallowed up in the water, and yet it exists—though not substantially, yet essentially. In its awakening, it is made known and becomes operative or active; everything would be a nullity or nothing, and an *Abyss*, without the Fire.

48. Thus we also understand that the Third Principle <note>The "Third Principle" refers to the physical, temporal world we inhabit.</note>—namely, the source or quality and the Spirit of this world—stood hidden from eternity in the nature of the Father's property. It was known by the light-flaming Holy Spirit in the *Holy Magic* <note>original: "Magia". This refers to the divine creative power or the wisdom that shapes reality.</note>—that is, in the *divine wisdom* and the Divine Tincture <note>The "Tincture" is the spiritual essence or "color" that gives life and quality to matter.</note>.

49. For the sake of *this*, the Deity moved itself according to the nature of the *Mother* <note>original: "Genetrix". This term refers to the birthing or generative power of nature.</note> and generated the Great Mystery, <margin>of the great mystery</margin> **wherein then *ALL* lay—whatever the Eternal Nature was able to do.**

50. And it was only a *Mystery*; it was *not* yet a creature, but a *Chaos*, Quintessence, mist, or mixture together.

51. Within this, the wrathful or fierce Nature generated a dark mist or cloud; and the light-flaming Nature in its property generated the *Flame* in Majesty and Meekness. This was the Water-source or quality, and the cause of divine *substantiality* from eternity.

52. And it is only virtue, power, and Spirit, which had no outward likeness; there are no footsteps of any physical thing within it. There was only the Spirit of God in a twofold source-quality and form: namely, a hot and a cold stern fire-source, and then a meek *Love-source* according to the nature of the Fire and of the Light.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of how the two properties—the Fire-source and the Light-source—interact within the divine "Great Mystery." # I. Part. Of the two Eternal Principles, Chap. 1.

<margin>Further details on the Mystery of the two Principles arising from two Properties</margin>

53. These have, as a *Mystery*, merged into one another, and yet one has not contained or fully grasped the other; instead, they have remained as if in two distinct Principles.

54. Within this, the "Astringency" <note>original: "Astringency" refers to the harsh, contracting force that Böhme identifies as the "Father of Nature."</note>—namely, the Father of Nature—has continually gathered or compressed "Substantiality" within the Mystery. There, it formed itself into something like an *Image*, and yet it was not a true image, but rather the *Shadow* of an image.

55. All of this within the Mystery has indeed always had an *Eternal beginning*. One cannot say there is anything that did not have its form or figure as a shadow within the eternal *Great Magia* <note>original: "Great Magia" refers to the divine creative power or potential that precedes physical manifestation.</note>.

56. But it was not yet a *Being* or *Substance*; it was a spiritual or divine play <note>original: "sport"; Böhme often describes the pre-creation state as a "play" or "joy-triumph" of the divine spirit.</note> within itself. This is the *Magia* of God’s great wonders, where what did *not* exist continually comes to be—where there was nothing but an *Abyss* <note>original: "Abysse" or *Ungrund*, the bottomless void before creation.</note>. Now, through the nature of Fire and Light, it has found a "Ground" or foundation.

57. And yet it comes from "Nothing," or only from the Spirit of the "source" or "quality." This spirit is not a substance either, but a driving quality <note>original: "source or quality" translates the German *Qual*, which implies a characteristic, a source, and a driving—sometimes painful—urge.</note> that generates itself within itself into *two properties* and also divides itself into *two principles*.

<margin>* Framer or Fashioner.</margin>

58. It has no external creator or "separator," but is its own cause. As is explained at length in other writings, the *Abyss* brings itself forth and generates itself into a "Ground."

<margin>Of the creation of Angels, men, and this world</margin>

59. In this way, we can understand the creation of this world, as well as the creation of Angels, humanity, and all other creatures. Everything is created out of the "Great Mystery."

60. For the "Third Principle" <note>The material world we live in.</note> existed before God as a *Magia* (a potentiality) and was not yet fully manifested or revealed.

61. Furthermore, God had no likeness or mirror in which He could perceive His own Being or Substance, except for *Wisdom*. Wisdom has been His longing delight, standing within His will and His Being as a *great wonder* in the light-flaming, divine *Magia* of the Spirit of God.

62. For Wisdom has been the dwelling place of the Spirit of God. She is not a *Genetrix* <note>original: "Genetrix" - a Latin term for a female parent or producer. Böhme means Wisdom does not "give birth" to things herself but reflects God's power.</note>, but rather the manifestation or revelation of God. She is a "Virgin" and the cause of divine substantiality.

<margin>Trinity</margin>

63. For within her stood the light-flaming divine *Tincture* <note>original: "Tincture" - a spiritual essence or transforming power.</note> directed toward the Heart of God—that is, toward the Word of Life of the Deity. She has been the revelation or manifestation of the *Holy Trinity*.

64. It is not that she reveals God through her own power or production; rather, the divine Center within God’s heart and being reveals itself *through* her. She is a *Mirror* <note>original: "Looking-Glass"</note> of the Deity.

65. For every *mirror* remains still and steady; it does not create an image, but reflects the image it receives. In this same way, the Virgin of Wisdom is a *mirror* of the Deity. In her, the Spirit of God sees itself, as well as all the wonders of the *Magia*, which came into *Being* or *Substance* with the creation of the Third Principle. Everything is created out of the "Great Mystery."

69. Understand that the *Father's Property* and the *First Principle* are found in the essence of the fire. In the quality or source of the light, understand the *Son's Nature*, which is the *Second Principle*. The driving Spirit coming out of both properties is the *Spirit of God*. In the First Principle, this spirit is fierce, wrathful, stern, bitter, cold, and fiery; it is the driving spirit within the Anger.

70. Therefore, it does not rest in fierce wrath and anger. Instead, it thrusts and blows forth from the essential fire so that it may unite itself again with the essence of the fire. The wrathful essences draw the spirit back into themselves, for it is their source of life. Yet, in the kindled fire, the spirit goes forth into the light—moving from the Father to the Son—and opens the fiery essences within the quality of the light.

71. There, the fiery essences are transformed by the great desire of burning Love. In this light-source, the first stern quality is not recognized as such; rather, the fierceness of the fire serves only as the cause of the light-flaming Majesty and the desiring Love.

72. This is how we are to understand the Being or substance of the Deity as well as Eternal Nature. We always recognize the Divine Being or substance within the light of the Majesty, for the gentle light makes the stern nature of the Father mild, lovely, and merciful.

73. Thus, he is called the *Father of Mercy* in relation to his Heart or Son. The Father's property consists of the nature of fire and light, and he himself is the Being of all beings or the substance of all substances.

<margin>Of the Trinity yet in two Principles</margin>
74. He is both the *Abyss* <note>original: "Abysse," the bottomless void before creation</note> and the *Ground* <note>original: "Bysse," meaning the foundation or base</note>. In the Eternal Birth, he divides himself into three properties as if into three Persons, and also into three Principles.

### The Second Chapter

->*Concerning the Revelation or Manifestation of the Mystery: How the Temporary Mystery has flowed forth out of the Eternal Spiritual Mystery.*<-

->1.<-

Since there has been a Mystery from eternity, we must now consider its manifestation or *revelation*. For we can speak of Eternity in no other way than as a Spirit.

2. For everything was originally only a Spirit, and yet from eternity, it has generated itself into Being or *Substance* through desiring and longing.

3. It cannot be said at all that in Eternity there was *no* Being or Substance; for no fire can exist without a substance to sustain it.

4. Furthermore, there is no gentleness <note>original: "Meekness," referring to the soft, light-filled quality of the divine</note> without the generation of Being or Substance. For gentleness generates *water*, and the fire consumes the water, making it—within itself—one part *Heaven* and Firmament, and the other part *Sulfur* <note>original: "Sulphur," an alchemical term for the combustible, active principle of substance</note>.

5. Within this, the fire-spirit, through its essential motion <note>original: "wheel"</note>, creates *Mercury* <note>original: "a Mercury," the alchemical principle of fluidity, communication, and transformation</note> and further awakens *Vulcan* <note>original: "the Vulcan," referring to the archetypal smith or the inner fire that shapes form</note>. That is, it strikes up the fire so that the third spirit—namely, the *Air*—is generated.

<margin>* Transparency or Reflection.</margin>

7. For the colors arise from the source-quality <note>Boehme uses the term "source" or "quality" to describe the fundamental forces of nature</note>. Black originates from the *harsh*, astringent ferocity; <margin>† The Forms of Nature.</margin> † all colors receive their specific qualities from this source-quality.

Within this, Nature exists in a state of sprouting, springing, and wrestling; the fire consumes that and also provides for it, and so it forms an Eternal Bond.

from the *Fire*, as if into *Inability*—that is, into *Being* or *Substance*.

16. For the Spirit arises in the Fire, but it splits itself into two sources or qualities: one into the *Fire*, and one in the *sinking down* into *Liberty*—into the *Light*.

17. This [Light] is called **God**; for it is meek and lovely, and contains the Kingdom of **Joy**. The angelic world is understood to exist within the *sunk-down liberty* of this Substantiality.

18. Therefore, when we departed from the liberty of the angelic essence <note>original: "Substantiality"</note> and entered the dark force <note>original: "source or quality"</note>—the core <note>original: "Abysse"</note> of which was the *Fire*—there was no *remedy*. This remained true until the Light's power and **Word**, acting as a word of Divine Life, became a Man. He brought us out of the darkness, through the fiery force, through the *Death* within that fire, and back again into the *Liberty* of the divine Life—into the divine Substantiality.

<margin>* Note.</margin>
19. Therefore, Christ had to die. With his soul-spirit, he had to pass through the Fire of Eternal Nature—namely, through *Hell and the fierce wrath of Eternal Nature—to enter into the Divine Substantiality. In doing so, he broke open a way for our souls through Death and Anger; through this path, *we may*—with him and in him—pass through death into Eternal Life.

20. But concerning divine Substantiality—that is, divine *Corporeity* <note>In Böhme’s thought, this refers to the "spiritual body" or the substantial reality of the heavenly realm</note>—we should understand it as follows:

21. We understand that the Light gives meekness, which is **Love**. Now, the anguish of the fire desires this meekness so that it may quench its great thirst. For the fire is full of desire, and the meekness is giving, for it gives of itself.

<margin>* Being or Essence <note>original: "Wesenheit"</note>.</margin>
22. Thus, through the desiring of meekness, *substance* or *Being* comes into existence—a substantial *Essentiality. This has "sunk down" away from the fierce wrath; it gives its own **Life** freely, and that is "Corporeity." Because of the power within that meekness, it becomes substantial; it is attracted, "put on," and held in place by the Astringency <note>The contracting, solidifying force</note> of the Eternal *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat," referring to God's creative command "let there be"</note>.

23. It is called Substantiality or Corporeity because it has "sunk down" from the fire-source and the Spirit. In relation to the spirit, it seems mute or inanimate—dead and powerless—and yet, it is an *Essential Life*.

24. Understand us correctly: when God created the Angels, there were only *Two* Principles manifested in Being or Substance. These were the principle in the Fire and the principle in the Light. One existed in the fierce, wrathful substantiality of the stern, contracting *Fiat*, featuring the forms of the fire’s nature.

25. The other existed in the heavenly substantiality, born of the Holy Power, featuring the water-source <note>A metaphor for the cooling, life-giving quality of the divine</note> of the Meekness of the Life of **Joy**. In this, the divine *Sulphur* <note>In alchemy and Böhme's philosophy, "Sulphur" represents the active, combustible principle of life and consciousness</note> was generated as **Love** and meekness; its *Fiat* was God’s desiring will.

### 3. Chapter: The Gate of the Creation of Man. Part I.

26. From *this* divine substance <note>original: "Substantiality"</note>—namely, out of God’s Nature—the angels were created as *creatures*. The source or quality of their spirit and life arises in the Fire.

27. For without Fire, no spirit can *exist* <note>original: "subsist"</note>. If it moves out of the Fire and into the Light, it gains the quality of love, and the fire becomes only the cause of its life; however, the fire’s ferocity is quenched by the Love in the Light.

28. But *Lucifer* despised this and remained in the fire-spirit. He elevated himself and ignited the substance in *his domain* <note>original: "his Place"</note>, which resulted in the creation of earth and stone. He was cast out, and so the *Third* Corporeity <note>the material world</note> and the Third Principle began, along with the kingdom of this world.

29. So, when the Devil was cast out into the darkness, God created *another* image in his own likeness in this place.

30. But if this image was to be God's likeness according to all *Three Principles* <note>In Böhme’s philosophy, the three levels of reality: the dark fire-world, the light world of God, and the visible material world</note>, then it had to be taken out of all *three*. It had to come from all beings or substances of this place or of *this "Deep"*, as far as the *Fiat* <note>original Latin: "let it be done"; God's creative command</note>—operating within Lucifer’s former domain—had extended itself into the ether during creation.

31. For humanity was created in the *place* of *Lucifer*. This is the source of the devils' envy; they cannot bear that humans have that honor. Instead, they continually lead humanity into the *evil* way of destruction to increase their own kingdom. They do this out of *spite* against meekness—namely, the love of God—believing that because they live in fierce, strong power, they are superior to the Spirit of God in love and meekness.

32. Understand it this way: God’s Will-Spirit—namely, the Holy Spirit—has enclosed the two-fold *Fiat* in two principles: the inward principle in the angelic world, and the outward principle in this world. And 

<margin>* Or Mass.</margin>
God created { the Mixture or Man <note>original German: "den Mesch oder Menschen"</note> } as a mixed person. For man was meant to be an image of both the inward and outward worlds, but he was intended to rule over the outward world through his inward quality. In this way, he would have been the likeness of God.

33. For outward substance was attached to the inward substance, and Paradise grew through the Earth. Man lived in Paradise while on the face of the Earth, for paradisiacal fruit grew for him until the Fall, when the Lord cursed the Earth.

34. Then Paradise passed into the Mystery <note>A hidden, spiritual dimension</note> and became a secret or hidden place to humanity. Yet, if a person is born of God again according to the inward man, he dwells in Paradise; however, according to the outward man, he dwells in this world.

35. We must further consider the *beginning* and *origin* of humanity:

41. The substance or matter out of which the body was created was a mass, or lump of fire and water, along with the * essences of both those principles, although the first principle also lay within it, but **without stirring**.

42. Every principle should remain in its own place and should not mix, just as it is in God; then man would be a **Total Image** according to God's being or substance.

# Of the Breathing-in of the Soul and of the Spirit.

43.
The body is an image <note>original: "similitude"</note> of God’s substance; the **soul** and **spirit** are an image of the Holy Trinity.

44. God gave the body its substance from the three principles; and the spirit, together with the soul, from the fountain of the threefold spirit of the all-being, all-substantial deity.

<margin>As God is in the spirit. verse 61.</margin>
45. And thus we are to understand that the soul, with its image and with its outward spirit, has proceeded out of three principles and was breathed and introduced into the body, as **Moses** witnesses: † *God breathed into man the breath of life into his nostrils, and so man became a living soul.* <note>Genesis 2:7</note>

46. But now the breath and spirit of God is threefold; that is, it exists in a threefold source or *quality*.

47. In the first principle, it is a fiery breath and spirit. This is the true cause of life and exists in the Father's source or quality—namely, in the center of the fierce, wrathful nature.

48. And then in the second principle, God’s breath or spirit is the light-flaming love-spirit—the true spirit of the actual Deity, which is called God the Holy Spirit.

49. And in the third principle, acting as a likeness of God, God’s breath is the air-spirit upon which the Holy Spirit rides. As *David* says:
<margin>* Psalm 18:10. † Genesis 1:2.</margin>
\**The Lord rides upon the wings of the wind*; and *Moses* says, † *The Spirit of God moved upon the waters*; that is, upon the enclosure <note>original Latin: *Capsula*; a small container or case</note> where the air arises.

50. Now, the total God, out of all three principles, has introduced and breathed this threefold spirit into the created image.

51. Namely: First, he introduced the fire-spirit into him from *within*—not through the nostrils, but in the heart, within the twofold tincture <note>original: "Tincture"; a fundamental spiritual quality or essence that "colors" or defines a substance</note> of the inward and outward blood. Although the outward blood was not known or perceived then (it was a mystery), the inward blood was active and had two tinctures: one from the fire and one from the light.

52. This fire-spirit is the true essential soul, for it holds the center of nature with its four forms for its fiery power. It strikes up the fire itself, and it creates the wheel of the essences <note>the fundamental qualities or "beings" that make up a thing</note> within itself, as is mentioned at length in the \* second and † third books.
<margin>\* *The Three Principles*. † *The Threefold Life*.</margin>

53. And you are to know that the essential soul-fire is not the true image according to the Deity. It is no image at all, but a *magical*, perpetually enduring fire.

### 54. It had *no* beginning; <insert>therefore</insert> it will also have *no* end.

55. And understand: God has introduced the eternal, beginningless fire—which has existed from eternity within itself in the eternal magic <note>original: *Magia*</note>, as the willing of God and the desiring of the eternal nature—as an eternal center of the Mother of Nature <note>original Latin: *Genetrix*; the generative or birthing power within nature</note>. This was done so that this image should be a likeness of him, or according to him.
<margin>Beyond why then the Spirit of God appeared when the spirit of the divine image was lost</margin>

56. And secondly, it is the same with the essential soul-fire: the Holy Spirit has introduced the light-flaming *love-spirit* out of itself, even in the second principle, where the Deity is understood.

57. This was not breathed in at the nostrils; rather, it was joined just as fire and light are attached to one another.

62. Thus, the soul creates Fire and Life, and the gentleness <note>original: "meekness"</note> of the Image creates Love and heavenly *substantiality*. In this way, the soul's fire becomes softened and satisfied with Love.

This can be seen in a lit fire: the *fire* in itself is a fierce, wrathful source or quality, while the *Light* is a gentle, lovely source or quality. And just as in the depths of this world, water comes to be out of Light and Air, it is the same here, as a likeness.

64. Thirdly, God has in like manner simultaneously breathed the *Spirit* of this world—with the source or quality of the Stars and Elements, namely the *Air*—into Man's *Nostrils*. That spirit should be a ruler in the outward Kingdom and **open the wonders of the** outward World; for this purpose, God also created Man in the Outward Life.

65. But the Outward Man should *not* reach into the Image.

### The Fourth Chapter.

### *Of the Paradisiacal* \* *Being, Substance, and Dominion: How it would have been if man had continued in innocence.*

->1.<-

The Devil has framed many objections by which he tries to **excuse** himself, saying that God **created** him *just as* he is; however, the angelic form which he *once* had always convicts him of being a liar.

2. And he always does the same to poor, fallen man: he constantly introduces the earthly kingdom, with its *power* and ability, into him, so that he may have a constant *looking-glass* [mirror] before him, leading him to also blame God as if He had created him earthly and evil.

3. But he leaves out the *best* parts, namely: first, the Paradise in which man was created; and then secondly, God's omnipotence—that † man does not live by bread alone, but also by the power and Word of God; and thirdly, that Paradise, with its source or quality, ruled over earthly things <note>original: "Earthlinesse"</note>.

4. He shows man only his hard, miserable, fleshly, naked form or condition. But he covers or conceals the condition of innocence—in which *Adam* did not know he was naked—in order to seduce man.

<margin>* Or carcass.</margin>

Although the earthly \* sack <note>original: "Sack"; a term used by Böhme to describe the physical body as a lowly vessel for the soul</note> is not worthy to know it, it is very necessary for our *minds* to know it.

6. Therefore, it is also necessary for us to fly to the true Doorkeeper *who has the key to open it*, to pray to him, and to yield ourselves wholly to him. We should ask him to graciously open the paradisiacal gate in the *inward center* of our image, so that the paradisiacal light might shine in our minds. In this way, we might long to dwell with our IMMANUEL again, as the *inward* and *new man* in Paradise.

14. And we see very well how we fall away and die when the outward heaven and its elements leave us. Even a child in its mother's womb is clearly old enough to die. Often it perishes while it is **still without life**, even while it is becoming a body through the <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat"; the creative command or "word" of God acting in nature</note> of the outward dominion, before the center of nature strikes up the fire of the soul.

15. Thus, through **Adam's** fall, we clearly recognize dying and death. As soon as **Adam** became earthly, he died to **Paradise** and was dead to the Kingdom of God.

otherwise, we could not become living again.

mixed, not to touch it; He also created only one man with both masculine and feminine properties, possessing both *tinctures* <note>original: "Tinctures"; in Jacob Böhme’s theology, these are the spiritual essences of fire (strength/soul) and light (love/spirit).</note>, both of the fire and of the light in love. Therefore, we cannot yield to human reason—which, through the Devil’s infection or instigation, claims that man was created as an earthly being.

17. For whatever was created solely from earthly life, or from earthly sources and qualities, is *bestial* <note>original: "Beastial"; meaning animal-like or belonging to the lower, physical nature.</note>. It has a beginning and an end and does not reach eternity, because it does not originate from eternity.

18. Now, anything that does not originate from eternity is *transitory*—it is merely a looking glass <note>original: "looking Glass"; a mirror.</note> in which the Eternal Wisdom has viewed itself as a *figure* and likeness.

19. Nothing remains of it except a *shadow* without source, quality, being, or substance. It passes away like a wind that rises and then dies down again.

20. The Word of God did not become flesh for the sake of such a creature; the Eternal did not enter into transitory substance for the sake of the transitory alone.

21. Furthermore, the Word did not enter into the earthly realm to raise or introduce the transitory earth into the power of God's Majesty. Rather, it was for the sake of *that* which had proceeded from the power of the Majesty—the human soul—which had become evil and earthly and was, as it were, *extinguished* in death. The Word came to make it living again, to awaken it, and to lift it up into the power of the Majesty, 
## into that state it was in, before it was a creature.

22. We must understand man *differently* than we have before, when we considered him merely animalistic. Indeed, he *became bestial* according to the properties of this world; when he died in *Adam*, from then on he lived for this world and not for God.

23. But if a person enters into God with their will-spirit <note>original: "will-spirit"; the core intent or orientation of the soul.</note>, then that will-spirit would regain the noble image once more. According to that image, they would *live* in God, while according to their bestial nature, they would live for *this world*.

24. Thus, he was in death and yet was living. Therefore, God's Word became man to unite him with God again, so that he might be *totally* born again in God.

25. We should conceive of the paradisiacal image in this way: we understand and believe that *Adam* was created *good*, pure, and immaculate—just as *Lucifer* and his hosts <note>original: "Hoasts"; the armies or companies of angels.</note> were.

<summary>Böhme argues that humanity was originally created as an eternal, spiritual being in Paradise, rather than a mere earthly animal. He explains that Christ’s incarnation serves to restore this lost "paradisiacal image" to the soul, which had become "bestial" and "extinguished" following the Fall.</summary>

48. 49. We can also sufficiently understand this through the food of the outward body: The outward man did indeed exist, yet he was, as it were, *half-swallowed up* by the inward man. The inward ruled entirely, and thus every aspect of life took its own food.

## The Fifth Chapter.
### Of the Lamentable and Miserable Fall of Man.

<center>->1.<-</center>

If we wish to rightly describe the Incarnation <note>original: "Becoming Man or Incarnation"</note> of JESUS CHRIST, it is necessary that we establish the *cause why God became man.*

<center>2.</center>

It is not a small cause, nor is it for nothing, as the Jews and the Turks view it. Even Christians are almost silent <note>original: "halfe dumb"</note> concerning it. Indeed, it must be a great cause for the unchangeable God to have moved himself. Therefore, observe this: we will lay out the *cause* for you.

<margin>
* Or, One.
† Note.
</margin>

<center>3.</center>

Adam was \* one <note>The marginal note suggests "One" as an alternative to "a"</note> man and \* an image of God, \* a complete likeness of God; although † **God is no image.** He is the *kingdom*, the *power*, as well as the *glory* and the *eternity*—All in All.

<center>4.</center>

Yet the "Deep without ground" <note>original: "the Deepe without ground"; referring to the *Ungrund*, a central concept in Böhme’s theology representing the absolute, unmanifested void of God’s essence before creation</note> longed or desired to manifest itself in *likenesses*, just as there were manifestations **which were done from eternity** in the wisdom of God, as in a virgin-like *figure.*

<center>5.</center>

This figure was not a birth-giver <note>original: "Genetrix"; a Latin term for a mother or a source of physical generation</note>, but a mirror of the *Deity* and of *eternity*, in the *Ground* <note>original: "Byss"; representing the manifest or established foundation of being</note> and in the *Abyss* <note>original: "Abyss"; the bottomless depth or the unmanifested</note>—an eye of the *glory* of God.

<center>6.</center>

And according to that Eye, and in that Eye, the thrones of princes were created—namely <note>original: "viz:"</note>, the angels—and in the end, Man. He likewise had the throne within himself, being created out of the eternal *magical power* <note>original: "Magia"; in Böhme's terminology, this refers to the divine creative will or the spiritual process of bringing something from nothing into being</note>, out of God’s being or substance, out of nothing into something, and out of spirit into body.

<center>7.</center>

And as the eternal *Magia* generated him out of itself into an *eye of the wonders* and *wisdom* of God, so he should and could have generated another man out of himself in a magical manner, without dividing or tearing his body.

<center>8.</center>

For he was conceived in God’s longing pleasure or delight, and—

### Reason's Objection

56. Human reason says: First, why did God allow the tree to grow by which Adam was tempted? Therefore, it must surely have been his will that Adam should be tempted.

57. Secondly: In this way, reason also attributes the Fall to God's will and assumes that God willed for Adam to fall. Thirdly: it assumes that God wills for some people to be in heaven and some to be in hell; otherwise, he could have prevented the evil and protected Adam so that he remained good and in Paradise.

58. This is also how the world judges today, for it says: *"If God had not created evil, nothing would be evil."* Seeing as everything has proceeded from him and he alone is the *Creator* who has made *all*, then he must have made both evil and good; otherwise, it would not be so. Reason will strictly maintain this position.

59. Also, reason thinks: if *those things* had not existed upon which the devil and man looked and *gazed*—becoming evil as a result—then the devil would have *remained* an angel and man would have remained in Paradise.

### Chapter 5: On the Miserable Fall of Man, Part 1

67. Eternal Light—its power and source <note>original: "source or quality"; refers to the essential nature of a thing</note>—dwells in the Light. The Light causes gentleness <note>original: "Meekness"</note>, and out of that gentleness comes being or substance. That being or substance is God’s being or substance, and the source of the Light is the Spirit of God, which is the *Understanding* <margin>* Original.</margin> there. There is no other God than this: the power is in the Light, and that power is the Kingdom.

68. But now, the Light and the Power have only a *love-will*; it does not desire evil. Indeed, it desires being or substance, but only from or out of its own essence. Understand that it comes out of love and *sweetness*, for that is consistent with the Light.

69. And yet, the Light arises from the fire, and *without the fire* it would be nothing; without it, the Light would have no essence. The fire creates life and mobility, and is *Nature*. Yet the fire has a different will than the Light, for it is greedy and only wants to consume; it only takes and receives, and climbs up high in *pride*.

70. The Light does not receive, but *gives*, so that the fire may be preserved. The quality of the fire is fierce wrath; its essences are *bitter*, and its sting is hostile <note>original: "enimicitious"</note> and unpleasant.

71. It is an enmity within itself; it consumes itself. **If the Light did not come to help it,** it would devour itself until nothing was left of it. Dear seeking mind, consider *this*, and you will soon reach the point of rest.

72. God is from eternity the Power and the Light, and He is called "God" according to the *Light*, according to the power of the Light, and according to the Spirit of the Light.

73. He is not called God according to the fire-spirit, for that is called His fierce wrath or His anger; it is not called God, but rather the consuming fire of the might and strength of God.

74. The fire is called *Nature*; the Light is not called Nature. It indeed has the properties of fire, but *changes* them from fierce wrath into love, from devouring and consuming into generating, and from enmity, hatred, bitter woe, and torment into gentle, well-doing, pleasant, and lovable desiring—a perpetual satisfaction and fulfillment.

75. For the desire for love draws the gentleness of the Light into itself and is a pregnant virgin—namely, with the wit, ingenuity, knowledge, and *wisdom* of the power of the Deity.

76. Thus it is clearly known to us what God and Nature are, as well as the *Byss and Abyss* <note>original: "Bysse and Abysse"; Böhme uses these terms to describe the "Ground" (foundation) and "Unground" (the bottomless nothingness/potential) of eternity</note>, and the deep of eternity. Thus we understand <margin>* Or the Ground</margin> that the eternal fire is *magical* <note>original: "Magical"; here meaning it is generated by the will or spirit rather than physical mechanics</note> and is generated in the desiring will, as is mentioned in the second and third books.

<margin>How the Devil and Adam were both free and that was their fall</margin>
80. The **Devil** was indeed an angel, and **Adam** was an image of God; they both had the **Fire** and the **Light**, as well as divine wit, ingenuity, or **understanding** within them. Why did the **Devil** direct his imagination toward the **Fire**, and **Adam** toward the Earth? They were **free**.

81. The Light and its power did not pull the Devil into the fire, but rather the fierce wrath of Nature did. Why did the Spirit consent to be willing?

## 82. Whatever the *Magia* <note>original: "Magia"; the creative power of the will or spirit</note> makes of itself, that is what it possesses.

The Devil made himself into Hell, and that is what he has; and Adam made himself into Earth, and that is what he is.

<margin>Concerning God as a Spirit and "opener," and how Fire and Light operate</margin>
83. God is not a creature, nor a "maker" <note>in the sense of a physical craftsman</note>, but a Spirit and an **Opener** <note>one who reveals or unlocks possibilities</note>. When the Creation occurred, we are to conceive of and understand it in this way:

<margin>The beauty of his own view <note>original Latin: "prospectu"</note>; he is within the creatures he formed. It has made nothing substantial <note>possessing physical matter</note> out of itself, for nothing else can exist besides it. 86. Yet no creature stands solely and barely in its essence. If a creature exists, it must be made out of a **substance**—namely, out of the power of "Sulphur." A creature must not be only spirit, but must also be "Sulphur" <note>In the alchemy of this period, Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt—the "Tria Prima"—represented the soul/will, the spirit/life, and the physical body/form respectively</note>.

...sulphur, in which the *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for 'let it be done,' referring to God's creative command</note> resides—that is, the sour *matrix* <note>original: "Matrix"; the womb-like source of nature</note> to the *center* of nature, where the spirit is preserved.

88. *That is*, it must be substance; for where there is no substance, there is also no *creating*. Even though a created spirit is not a tangible substance, it must draw substance into itself through its imagination; **otherwise, it would not exist.**

89. *So then*, if the Devil drew fierce wrathfulness into himself, and Man drew in earthliness, what could the love of God’s substance do about that? The Devil certainly had the love and meekness of God, along with the divine substance, *set before him* and offered to him—as was also the case with Man. Who, then, can blame **God**?

90. But the fierce, wrathful *essence was too strong*, so that it overcame the essence of love. What can God do about that? If a healthy branch is planted and then withers, what can the earth do? The earth provides sap and strength; why does the branch *not* draw those qualities into itself?

91. You might say its essences are *too weak*, but what can the earth do about that? And what can the person who planted that branch do? His will is to produce a good tree for his pleasure and delight, and he would like to eat its fruit. But if he knew the branch would *wither*, he would never have planted it.

92. Thus we should understand that the angels were not created like a person planting a tree. Instead, they were created through the *movement* of God, involving both principles—Light and darkness—within which the fire lay hidden. Yet, during the creation and the movement, the fire *did not burn*, just as it does not burn today [in that divine state], for it has a principle of its own.

93. Why did Lucifer kindle *that* fire? The will existed **within his created being**, not outside or beyond him. He wanted to be a lord over fire and light; he wanted to extinguish the Light and despised the divine meekness, wishing instead to be a *Fire-Lord*.

94. And when he despised the Light and his birth in meekness, he was *justly thrust out*. Thus, he left the true Fire and Light and must now dwell in the abyss of darkness. If he wants fire, he must strike it up for himself and kindle it with his own malice or malignity in his <margin>malice or *evilness*</margin> *imagination*.

# The Sixth Chapter.

### *Concerning Adam's Sleep: How God created a Woman out of him; how he became entirely Earthly; and how God, by the Curse, has withdrawn Paradise from him.*

->I.<-

When Man became weary and tired, he fell into a sleep—namely, into the *Magia* <term>original: "Magia"; Jacob Boehme uses this term to describe the creative, spiritual power of the will or imagination</term>. It was for him as if he were not in this world, for all his senses or thoughts ceased, and the wheel of his *essences* <term>original: "Essences"; the fundamental spiritual qualities or energies that make up a being</term> came to a rest.

2. He was, so to speak, essential rather than substantial; he was completely like the *Magia*, for he knew nothing of his body. He lay there as if dead, but was not truly dead; rather, the spirit <margin>The Spirit of the Body.</margin> stood still.

3. And then the essences have their *effect*, and only the spirit of the soul sees or discerns; and whatever the starry heaven brings forth is then *portrayed* in the sidereal <term>original: "sydereal"; relating to the stars or the celestial, astrological influences on the soul</term> spirit.

4. This stood magically in the mind like a looking-glass, which the spirit of this world † *gazes* upon <margin>† Or is overcome with gazing; to qualify or operate.</margin>. It conveys whatever it sees in the looking-glass into the *essences*, and the *essences* flow into them, as if they were performing the work and portraying it in the spirit. These are what we call *dreams*, representations, or *figures*.

5. Thus, we should know that when earthliness wrestled with Adam and he turned his imagination toward it, he was instantly infected by it. His *mind* became dark and stern.

6. For earthliness began to qualify—or operate—like water that begins to boil over a fire. The source or quality of the stars became active and now became the masters of his **body**.

7. And now Moses says quite rightly † that God caused a deep sleep to fall upon him <margin>† Genesis 2:21.</margin>. This means that because his will-spirit imagined after earthly things, God let him fall; for through his imagination, he brought earthliness upon himself.

5. If Christ had brought a soul from heaven, what then would happen to our souls? And what would become of the covenant made with Adam and Eve—namely, that <margin>* Genesis 3:15</margin> the seed of the woman should crush the serpent's head?

# The Ninth Chapter.

### Concerning Mary's Virginity: what she was before the blessing, and what she became through the blessing.

-> I. <-

1. It is highly necessary for us, the poor children of Eve, to know this; **for our eternal salvation lies within it.** It is the gate of *Immanuel* <note>Hebrew: "God with us"</note>, and the entire Christian faith stands upon it; it is also the gate to the greatest secret *arcanum* <note>original: "arcanum" — a deep, hidden mystery or secret knowledge</note>.

2. For within this is enclosed the secret of humanity, in that man is the likeness and image of God; for our whole religion consists of *three parts*, which we emphasize and teach.

3. *First*, concerning the *Creation*: what essence, substance, and property humanity is; whether he is eternal or not; and how that is possible—what the human origin truly is, from which he proceeded in the beginning.

4. *Secondly*: Seeing as much is spoken and taught concerning his *Fall*, and we see that we have become mortal because of that fall—moreover, *subjected* to evil and to the fierce, wrathful source—what, then, his fall truly was.

5. *Thirdly*: Since God will receive us into *grace* again, and for whose sake he has also given the Law and *teachings*—confirming them with deeds of wonder or *miracles*—what the new regeneration truly is.

6. And since we see that we *must die*, by what power and spirit we can be newly regenerated and rise again from death.

14. Thus, the earthly quality destroyed the heavenly and ### became the *disturbance* <note>original: "Turba" — Latin for "turmoil" or "uprising"; in this context, it refers to a disruptive force that brings corruption and death.</note> of the heavenly.

The *creative word* <note>original: "Fiat" — Latin for "let it be done," referring to God's command in Genesis.</note> has made earth and stones out of the heavenly substance.

# Chapter 9: On Mary’s Virginity, Part 1

God has revealed himself within humanity; specifically, through his Son becoming man in the Incarnation.

### 25. And so, in our imagination,

which we focus <note>original: "introduce"</note> on his becoming man, we become filled <note>original: "impregnated"</note> with his revealed Word and the power of the **heavenly** and divine substance. This is not at all something foreign to us, yet it seems foreign to our earthly nature.

<margin>The dead life has been awakened in every person. Christ is risen. This is the first resurrection.</margin>

26. The Word has revealed itself everywhere, even in the "light of life" within every person; and the only thing missing is for the soul-spirit to surrender itself to it. In doing so, it puts on eternal virginity again—not as a garment, but as something arising from its own essence. *And in that soul-spirit, God is generated or born.*

27. For Mary, along with all of Eve’s daughters, was born earthly; but the Covenant of God’s love showed within their essence that God would reopen life there once again.

28. We cannot say that Mary’s virginity—in terms of her earthly life before the Blessing, before God’s Heart moved itself—was a totally perfect virginity like that before the Fall; she was a natural daughter of Eve.

<margin>This explains the possibility of the inner man being born by the power of the Spirit in every child of Adam. This is the light that lights every person who comes into the world.</margin>

29. But we say with good reason that in Mary, as in all of Adam’s children, eternal virginity has lain shut up as if in death within the Covenant of Promise; yet in God, it has not faded.

30. For the name **Jesus**, in the center or Heart of God, has from eternity reflected itself in the Virgin of God’s wisdom as if in a mirror <note>original: "Looking-Glass"</note>. It has stood before the Father’s center—that is, the center of fire and fierce wrath—not within the fierce wrath of that essence, but in the Light within the Light's essence.

<margin>A kindling of that which died in Adam.</margin>

33. And so now, according to our deep knowledge, we say of **Mary**: that before the time of the revelation and the message of the Angel, she was a virgin just as Eve was when she left Paradise.

34. Before Adam knew her, Eve was indeed a virgin; however, the true, spiritual virginity had perished in her and was infected with earthly longing.

### Question.

<margin>Question</margin>
36. Now Reason asks: How did this happen in the process of becoming Man, or the Incarnation? Did the Life suddenly become active at the moment of conception, beyond the natural course, so that the portion of Mary—namely, the woman's seed—instantly lived?

### Answer.

<margin>Answer</margin>
37. No: for it was a substantial seed, and it became active with Soul and Spirit in its natural time, just like all of Adam's children.

38. But that part of the Deity, surrounded by divine substantiality <term>substantiality: Böhme uses this to describe the "heavenly flesh" or spiritual matter that makes up the divine realm.</term> and wisdom, lives from eternity to eternity.

39. The Deity did not move here or there; what it *was*, it remained, and what it *was not*, that it became.

40. It gave itself with divine substantiality into the essence and substantiality of Mary; and Mary’s essence and God’s essence became <insert>one Son.</insert>
<margin>* Or Person.</margin>

41. But Mary's essences were *mortal*, but God’s essences were *immortal*.

42. Therefore, Mary’s essences had to **die on the Cross** and pass through death into life. God’s essences helped with this; otherwise, it would have been impossible.

43. Thus, God’s essence helped us, and still always helps us through Christ, to return into God’s essence and life once more.

<header>Chapter 11: Of the Profit of Christ's Incarnation. Part 1.</header>

# The Eleventh Chapter

### *Regarding the benefit and profit of the Incarnation <note>original: "Becoming Man"</note> and birth <note>original: "Geniture"</note> of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, for us poor children of Eve.*

# The most rich, lovely gate of all.

->1.<-

We poor children of Eve were all dead in Adam; and though we appeared to live, yet we *lived only* for this world, and death *waited* for us and continually devoured us one after another. There would have been no remedy for us if God had not birthed <note>original: "Generated"</note> us again out of his own substance.

2. As far as the *body* is concerned, we would never have returned in eternity, and our *soul* would have eternally continued in the source of God's anger alongside all the devils.

3. But the Incarnation of Jesus Christ has become a powerful substance or *matter* for us; for God became man for our sakes, so that he might bring our humanity out of death back into himself and **redeem or release our soul** out of the fire of God's anger.

<margin>* Or towards.</margin>
4. For the soul in *itself* is a source of fire <note>original: "Fire-source or quality"</note> and contains within itself the *First Principle*—the harsh astringency <note>In Böhme's philosophy, "astringency" is the contractive force of the first "dark" principle of nature.</note> which, by itself, works only * toward the fire.

5. But if the love and meekness of God are withdrawn from this soul's birth, or if the soul becomes infected with a totally harsh <note>original: "stern"</note> matter, then it continues as a source of torment in the darkness—a totally harsh roughness, devouring itself while also, in the hunger of its will, always generating itself again.

<summary>Böhme explains that without Christ's incarnation, humanity would remain trapped in a self-devouring cycle of spiritual fire and anger. Through the Incarnation, God provides a new spiritual substance to redeem the soul from its natural "harshness" and return it to divine love.</summary>

<margin>How the soul has and has not a beginning</margin>
9. For a thing that has no beginning or ground <note>In Böhme's philosophy, "ground" refers to an underlying cause or foundation.</note> also has no end; but it is its own ground and generates itself.

7. And yet we will not say that the soul has no beginning; it has a beginning, but only as a created being <note>original: "according to the Creature"</note>, not according to its essence: **its essence is from eternity.**

8. For the divine *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat," the Latin word for "let it be," representing God's creative command.</note> has encompassed it in the center of eternal nature and brought it into a substantial <gloss>Substance</gloss>; moreover, with the whole cross, with the *character* of the **Holy Trinity**, as an image <note>original: "Similitude"</note> of the threefold spirit of the Deity, wherein God dwells. Now, whether it be done in love or anger—that is, in light or fire—it becomes pregnant with whichever of those it focuses its imagination upon. For the soul is a magical spirit; it is a source or quality within itself.

9. Thus it is the center of eternity, a fire of the Deity in the Father, yet *not* in the Father's liberty <note>Böhme uses "liberty" to describe God's state of pure freedom beyond all manifestation.</note>, but in eternal nature.

<margin>† Come to be.
* Outside <note>original: "Extra"</note>.</margin>

<margin>Of the liberty of God — within and without substance</margin>

12. And there would be no God without the substance, but only an eternal stillness without source or quality.

13. But within the source or quality, the fire is generated, and out of the fire, the light. There, *two* substances separate themselves and drive forward a twofold *source* or *quality*: namely, a fierce, wrathful, hungry, and thirsty one in the fire, and a meek, lovely, yielding, and giving one in the light.

<margin>Fire and light: their twofold properties</margin>
14. For the light gives, and the fire takes away. The light gives meekness, and out of that meekness comes "substantiality" <note>This refers to a spiritual "body" or matter.</note>, which is the fire's food; otherwise, the fire would be a dark, fierce, wrathful hunger within itself.

15. As indeed a spirit *is*, if it does not have the substance of the light; it is like a loathsome poison.

16. But if it *attains* the substance of meekness, then it attracts that into itself and dwells therein, using it for food and also for its body. For it affects or fills <note>original: "infecteth"</note> itself with it and makes itself pregnant with it; for its substance is its satisfaction or fulfillment, and thus its hunger becomes stilled.

This is called faith, or believing.

<margin>Fire, light, and spirit are the outward manifestation of the hidden God, in which consists his Kingdom of Heaven. The union of these three principles constitutes heaven; their division (which can only take place in a created being) is hell. To the angels, God is a spirit of splendor, light, and love. To the devils, he is a consuming fire—that is, fire separate and apart from the light, which is the glory of the fire, just as the fire is the strength and power of the light. The union of the fire with its light, spirit, Holy Spirit, and Word constitutes the life, the light, and the love of the Kingdom of Heaven.</margin>

46. This fire also does not become manifest in the pure Deity, for the light has swallowed up the fire into itself and gives the fire its love, its substance, and its water, **so that in God's substance there is only love**, joy, and a pleasant dwelling place, and no fire is perceived.

47. But the fire is only a cause of the desiring will and of the love, as well as of the light and of the majesty; otherwise, there would be no substance. This has been extensively explained in former writings.
