# Chapter 5

->*Why the wicked do not convert. What the most painful thing in converting is. Of the false pastors or shepherds. Of the Tree of Faith. How a person must enter into the Kingdom of God. Of the breaking of the Kingdom of Lucifer. Of the three forms of life: and what we have inherited from Adam and from Christ.*<-

---

->1.<-

The wicked multitude cannot conceive or understand all of this, and the reason is this: there is **no will** in them that desires to understand it.

2. For earthly substance has captivated *them*, so that they cannot create or form any will toward God’s Mystery <note>original: "Mistery"; in Boehme’s theology, the hidden spiritual essence of reality or the divine foundation</note>. They are like the *dead* to God; there is no breath of divine life in them, and they *desire* nothing of it. They are locked up within the Mystery of God’s anger, so that they do not know *themselves*.

3. God has not done this to them; instead, they have entered into it with their own spirit of will and have so *immersed* <note>original: "demersed"; meaning to be plunged or sunk into something</note> themselves. Therefore, they continue on like madmen.

4. Yet the **noble jewel within them remains hidden** in the noble center, in the divine principle; and they *are* very much able, through their will, to go out from the earthly substance and malice or wickedness, and enter into the will of God.

5. But they willfully and obstinately let that fierce wrath *hold* them; for the proud, stately life of self-honor pleases them *too much*, and that also holds them captive.

# Chapter 5: What is Most Painful in Conversion. Part III.

6. But after this life, there is no remedy anymore. When the soul's fire is purely and barely naked, it can be quenched by nothing except God's meekness—with the water of eternal life in the Mystery of God. However, the souls in that state *do not* reach or attain that water; <margin>* Luke 16:26</margin> for afterwards, there is a *great cliff or gulf between them*, representing an entirely different Principle <note>original: "Principle"; in Boehme's thought, a "Principle" is a fundamental realm of existence, such as the world of light, the world of darkness, or the physical world</note>.

<margin>† Psalm 18:10</margin> 7. But in this present time, while the soul swims and burns in the blood <note>Referring to the soul's current connection to the physical body and living spirit</note>, it may well be reached, for the Spirit of God † *goes upon the wings of the wind*; God has become Man.

8. The Spirit of God goes *with those who are willing* into the soul; it desires the soul. It sets its **Magia** <term>Magia: a term used by Boehme to describe the spiritual power of the will to attract, create, or be shaped by divine or earthly influences</term> toward <margin>* Revelation 3:20</margin> the soul. The soul needs only to *open the door*, and then the Spirit goes in voluntarily and opens the noble grain for the Tree of the Christian Faith.

9. But this is the most painful part, which enters most bitterly into a person: he must break off the "willing-spirit" from earthly substance. He must bring forth the willing-spirit out of its earthly treasure—namely, out of pride, pomp, covetousness, and envy, as well as out of anger and falsehood—toward the Spirit of God.

10. His mouth must not be that of a hypocritical flatterer while his heart and will remain stuck in the earthly mystery. He must be *sincere* and earnest from the ground of his heart and soul.

11. The *will* must turn itself around into the Divine Mystery—namely, into God’s love—so that the Spirit of God may have space and place within it to fan the divine *spark*. Otherwise, there is no remedy; no flattering hypocrisy will do it.

<margin>* Note.</margin> 12. * And even if one should learn *all the Scriptures* by heart, by rote, and should sit all his life long in the church, yet still remains in the soul's image an earthly, beast-like man—who in his heart hunts only after falsehood, deceit, and wickedness—then his flattering hypocrisy will help him not at all.

13. A preacher who handles God's Mystery externally in the outward world, and yet does not have God's image internally in the inward world, but only seeks after honor and greed, is as near to the Devil as the lowliest of all. He is only a juggler <note>original: "Jugler"; meaning a deceiver, trickster, or someone who manipulates things for show</note> with God's Mysteries, and a hypocrite without power.

14. He himself does not possess the Mystery, so how *will* he give or <margin>* Ephesians 6:19</margin> dispense it to others? He is a false shepherd and † *a wolf among the sheep.* <margin>† Matthew 7:15</margin>

15. For every person who bears the Mystery of God—that is, who has awakened or stirred it up and surrendered himself to it—does so in such a way that

### Part III. What is Most Painful in Conversion. Chapter 5.

58. And this is the core reason: that as we, with *Adam*, left this Life and entered the Outward Life—which is also why God became Man—He must lead us back *through* this death, through and out of the fierce, wrathful source or quality of the **fire-anguish-life**, and through Death into the **light-and-love-life** once again.

61. For by that stronghold, Lucifer *thought* he would be a Lord and an omnipotent Prince.

63. Thus, the Light and the Love have entered into the Anger, together with the Paradise-Element and the water of Eternal Life, and God’s anger has been *quenched*.

64. And so now Lucifer remains within himself in an anxious, fierce, wrathful fire-source, where *his* body is a poison, a source of poisonous water.

65. And thus, he has been thrust out from God’s fire into the *Matrix* <note>original: "Matrix of the Eternal Nature"; the "womb" or originating ground of nature’s forces</note> of Eternal Nature—that is, into the stern harshness which generates eternal darkness. There he manages a very stern dominion in the anxious *Mercurius* <term>Mercurius: In Boehme's thought, the restless, driving, and often "anxious" force of motion and life within the qualities of nature</term>, and so he exists as a **reproach or an outcast.**

66. He who in his origin was a Prince is now no more than an executioner, a base slave, who must remain in God's fierce wrath as a hangman. He *punishes* the evil when he is commanded by his Lord to do so; he has no power beyond that.

67. Although he is still a *deceiver* who seeks to entrap many so that his kingdom may be large, so that he may have many followers and not stand in reproach with so few.

### Chapter 5. What is Most Painful in Conversion. Part III.

68. Just as a prostitute thinks, "If there were many prostitutes, then I would not be a **prostitute alone**; I am just like the others," he [Lucifer] also desires a great tribe or ancestry so that he may reproach God.

69. For he always attributes the blame and fault for his fall to God, claiming that God's wrath drew him in and thrust him into such a state of pride and will that he could not remain standing.

70. Thus he assumes that if he could draw many others to himself, his kingdom would be great. He would gain more followers who would do as he does: curse God while justifying themselves. That is his strength and pleasure in his dark, harsh anguish, where he continually stirs up the fire within himself and tries to fly out above the heavenly Thrones, still considering himself to be a Prince and King.

71. And though he is indeed evil, he is a Prince among his legions within the Anger inside his own being <note>original: "Creature"</note>. However, regarding the **Anger outside** of his being, he has **no power** to act; in that realm, he must remain as a helpless captive.

72. Thus, understand Life in *two* forms: *one* according to the fire of Nature, and the *other* according to the fire of Light. This Light-fire burns in Love, and it is within this Love that the Noble Image of God appears or shines.

<margin>* Colossians 3:3</margin>
73. And we understand here that the human will should enter into God’s will. In this way, a person goes through Christ’s death with Christ’s soul—*through Death*—into the Eternal Liberty of God and into the life of Light. *There, he is in Christ with God.* <note>Colossians 3:3: "For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God."</note>

# The Sixth Chapter.

### *What Lust can do: How we fell in Adam and are helped again in Christ, and why it is no easy matter to become a true Christian.*

->1.<-

Thus we understand that the problem lies in lust; that destruction or ruin came out of lust, and yet it still comes from there continually.

2. For <term>lust</term> is a process of imagining, where the <term>imagination</term> winds or inserts itself into all forms of nature, so that they all become impregnated with the thing that the lust is focused on. <note>original: "Imagining... Imagination"—Here, these terms refer to the creative power of the mind and will to shape one's internal spiritual reality.</note>

3. As we then understand, the outward spirit of man—which is a likeness of the inward spirit—has lusted after the fair Image. In that regard, it has set **its imagination** into the inward spirit, which has caused the inward to become * infected.
<margin>* Influenced or colored. <note>original: "Affected or Tincted." In alchemy and Boehme's theology, a "tincture" is a transformative quality that changes the nature of a substance.</note></margin>

4. And because it did *not instantly* feel death, it gave space and room to the outward spirit within its <term>willing-spirit</term>. Thus, the outward was drawn into the inward to find lodging, eventually becoming the *host* in the house. This has obscured or dimmed the inward spirit, so that the fair Image has disappeared.

5. Then the Image fell among murderers—namely, among the stern or severe spirits of nature and of the origin of life. These held the Image captive, stripped it of its <term>Paradise Garment</term>, <note>The "Paradise Garment" represents the spiritual body or robe of light that humans possessed before the Fall.</note> committed murder within it, † and left it *lying half-dead*.
<margin>* Note: These are the spirits Cain was afraid of. See *The Great Mystery* (original: Mysterium Magnum), chapter 29, verse 55.</margin>
<margin>† Luke 10:30.</margin>

6. And now the *Samaritan*, Christ, was needed; that is the reason why God became human.

7. If the wound or injury could have been healed simply by speaking a word or by a verbal forgiveness, God would not have needed to become human.

9. And so God came with his Word—which is the center of the life of light—<gloss>and became flesh</gloss>, so that the soul received a divine, paradisiacal home once again. It should be understood in this way:

10. Just as Adam's soul had opened the door to the **fire's essences** <note>original: "Fires Essences"—In Boehme's cosmology, the "fire" represents the harsh, driving, and potentially wrathful energy of nature that must be tempered by light.</note> and had let in the earthly essences—whose qualities wound themselves into the Paradise-image and made the image earthly—

11. —so God's heart set open the doors of the **light's essences** and surrounded the soul with heavenly flesh. Thus, the essences of the holy flesh took their form from the Image, according to the essences of the soul.

12. In this way, the soul became "impregnated" again, so that its <term>willing-spirit</term> <note>original: "willing-spirit"—The part of the human spirit that directs the will and desire.</note> could pass through death into the life of Paradise.

13. This led to the temptation of Christ; he was tempted to see whether the soul would "eat" of the Word of the Lord and whether it could enter through death into the life of God.

14. This was ultimately fulfilled on the wood of the **Cross**, where Christ's soul went through the fire of fierce wrath, through the harsh source, and through death, and then sprouted forth again into the **holy Paradise-world** in which Adam was first created.

15. Thus we human beings have been helped again. It is necessary for us to draw our will, thoughts, and mind away from all earthly things and turn them toward Christ's suffering, dying, death, and resurrection.

16. We must continually crucify the "old Adam" <note>original: "Old Adam"—The fallen, sinful nature of humanity inherited from the first man.</note> through Christ's death and continually die to sin in the death of Christ. We must also continually rise again with him out of the anguish of death as a "new man" and sprout into the life of God; otherwise, there is no remedy.

17. We must die to our earthly will within our own will and be continually reborn into the **new world** through faith in the flesh and blood of Christ. We must be born out of Christ's flesh if we wish to see the Kingdom of God.

<header>III. Part. Why this World and all Things were Created. Chap. 7.</header>

# The Seventh Chapter.

->*For what purpose this world and all substances or things were created. Also, concerning the two eternal mysteries; the mighty struggle in man over the image; and where the tree of Christian faith stands, grows, and bears fruit.*<-

---

->1.<-

Since man exists in this way within a *threefold life*, each life is a mystery or hidden secret <term>Arcanum</term> <note>original: Arcanum; a secret or hidden mystery</note> to the others and desires them. For this reason, the world and all its substances or things were created.

2. For divine substance desires a reflection or likeness, and this world is a likeness according to God's being or substance.

3. God is made manifest in an earthly likeness because the wonders of the hidden secret <term>Arcanum</term> <note>original: Arcanum</note> could not be revealed in the angelic world or in the "Love-Birth" <note>The "Love-Birth" refers to the divine generation of the spiritual world through love.</note>.

4. But in this world, where love and anger are mixed, there exists a twofold producer <term>Genetrix</term> <note>original: Genetrix; a Latin term meaning "mother" or "producer," used here to describe the creative or generating power of nature.</note>, and there it was possible.

5. For all things originally arise from the "fire-root," yet they were surrounded by the "water of meekness," so that it is a pleasant or lovely substance or being.

6. However, the fire was not known in the angelic world because the center of the producer <term>Genetrix</term> <note>original: Genetrix</note> stands in the light and is the Word of God. Thus, the wonders of nature can only be seen in God's wisdom through a spiritual magic <term>Magia</term> <note>original: Magia; referring to the creative, supernatural power through which the spirit acts upon matter.</note>.

7. But since this is almost incomprehensible to angels and the souls of men, and yet God desires to be known in them, the angelic world longs to know the great **wonders** that have existed from eternity in the wisdom of God.

It describes how the angelic world longs to understand these divine wonders which are fully known only through God's wisdom.</summary>

20. And *secondly*, we are to ponder and consider the desire for Love, which originally arises in the Word of Life within the Angelic World, where the heart of God stands toward us with His desire.

20. And *secondly*, we must ponder and consider the desire for Love, which originally arises from the Word of Life in the Angelic World, where the Heart of God, with His desire, stands toward us

He explains the internal struggle of nature to move from the "anguish" of the fire-center toward the "meekness" and liberty of divine Light.</summary>

# ...us with his imagining, and also draws us into the divine Mystery.

21. And then, *thirdly*, we are to consider the **Magick Kingdom** <term>Magick Kingdom</term> <note>In Boehme's theology, "Magic" refers to the spiritual power of the Will to bring thoughts into substance or reality.</note> of this world, which also burns in us and vehemently draws us into its wonders; for it desires to be manifested.

22. And Man was created within it for that end: that he should manifest that same Mystery and bring the **Wonders to light** and into forms according to the eternal wisdom.

23. Now, since he is to do this, and because he burns in a threefold fire <note>The "threefold fire" refers to the three principles: the dark/wrathful fire, the light/divine fire, and the earthly/outward fire.</note>, the true Spirit—in which the **Angelical Image** <note>The "Angelical Image" is the pure, spiritual essence of man as intended by God.</note> resides—suffers great weariness and is in great danger, for it wanders upon a very narrow bridge.

24. For it has *two* enemies which continually pull at it; each wants to be in the Image and bring its source-like <note>original: "sourceive," meaning the fundamental, springing quality of a thing's nature.</note> quality into it. These are the *inward fire* and also the *outward fire*—the inward Kingdom of fierce wrath, and also the outward earthly Kingdom of the looking-glass <note>The "looking-glass" is the material world, which reflects the eternal spiritual realities in a temporary form.</note>. Thus, the true Image sits in the middle, in the * squeezing press.
<margin>* Crushing/Squeezing <note>original: "Quetzung," a German term Boehme uses for the pressure or "shaping" force of existence.</note></margin>

25. For the inward Kingdom *will*, through the outward, reveal its wonders.

26. But because the inward is too sharp <note>original: "sharp," meaning intense, harsh, or overwhelming.</note>, the outward Kingdom flees from the inward and grasps for the middle part—namely, for the Image, which stands in the **Liberty of God** <note>The "Liberty of God" refers to the divine stillness or the "Nothing" from which all things emerge.</note>. Thus, the outward world flees and slips itself into the Image, for everything reaches for the heart of God, which is the center of the Kingdom of Joy.

27. Therefore, it is now necessary for the Image to defend itself and not let in the earthly guest, much less the fiery one; and yet the Image is generated out of *both*: the life from the fire, and the wonder from the outward world.

28. Therefore, it is highly necessary for Man's Image that he lead
<margin>* 1 Peter 5:8.</margin>
* **a sober, temperate life** and not fill himself with the outward Kingdom; otherwise, it establishes a dwelling-place within the noble Image.

29. And we understand here the mighty struggle in Man concerning the Image of God. For there are *three* that strive for it: *first*, the stern, strong fire-life; *secondly*, the divine life; and *thirdly*, the earthly life. And so, the noble Image sits in the middle and is pulled by all three.

30. Now, it is necessary for the Image to hide itself with faith in the mystery of hope and to stand still within that same mystery.

31. Thus, the Devil, dwelling in the inward fire-life, continually rides forth into the *outward* earthly life—driven by pride, covetousness, and falsehood or wickedness—against the Noble Image <note>The "Noble Image" is the divine spark or true spiritual identity of a human being as intended by God.</note>. He seeks to drag it into the fire and life of anguish, and to break or destroy it.

32. For he continually supposes that the place of *this world* is his kingdom, and he will tolerate no other image within it.

33. Consequently, the Noble Image falls into the Cross and tribulation, into anguish and necessity. Here, it must struggle to fight for the Noble *victorious* Crown or garland of God's Image.

<margin>Of the rise of prayer</margin>
34. And this is the original source of **Prayer**: so that the Image continually goes out from the earthly substance or being it has taken on, and also out of proud, worldly, and hellish abominations, through prayer; it continually enters into God's life, into His **Love**.

35. In this way, the true Image continually kills the earthly Adam <note>The "earthly Adam" refers to the fallen, physical human nature focused on worldly desires.</note>, as well as the hellish pride and status of the Devil, and must always stand as a *champion*.

<margin>Of the necessity of patience</margin>
36. And it is most necessary of all that the Image should immerse itself in **Patience**, casting itself under the Cross, and continually springing or flowing up into Love.

37. For that Love is its *sword*, with which it slays the Devil and drives out the earthly substance. It has no other sword to defend itself with than the meek water of Eternal Life. The proud, haughty, fierce, and wrathful spirit does not relish this water; for it is his poison, and he flees from it.

38. Now, if we are to correctly describe the *Tree of Christian Faith*, we say: its root stands in the mystery of **Hope**, its sprouting stands in **Love**, and its body or trunk in the *comprehension of Faith. <margin>* Or reception</margin>

39. That is, when the Image—through its earnest desire—presses into the love of God and comprehends or *attracts* the substantiality of God, which is *Christ's body* <note>original: "Corpus," referring to the divine substance or spiritual presence of Christ.</note>. That is the body in which the tree stands, grows, flourishes, and brings forth fruit in patience, all of which belong to the angelical world.

40. These fruits are the soul's food, upon which it eats and refreshes or quickens its fiery life, so that it is transmuted or changed into **Light** or meekness.

<margin>† Note: The outward man, and reason, do not know the Tree of Faith.</margin>
41. And thus the tree grows in the Paradise of God, which the **outward man † does not know, and Reason does not grasp.**

<margin>1 Peter 5:8</margin>
44. In this world, the pilgrim is only in a valley of misery and must constantly live in conflict. For "the Devil prowls around like a roaring lion" <margin>1 Peter 5:8</margin>; he stirs up all his children of malice and wickedness against the believer.

# The Eighth Chapter.

### *How God Forgives Sins, and How a Person Becomes a Child of God.*

---

->1.<-

<margin>* Matthew 5:6</margin>
My beloved, seeking, and longing mind—you who *hunger* and *thirst* for God's kingdom: please pay attention to the fundamental truth <note>original: "Ground"</note> that is shown to you here.

2. Truly, it is not as easy a thing to become a child of God as *Babel* <note>The author uses "Babel" (referring to the Tower of Babel) as a metaphor for the confused and worldly institutional churches of his time.</note> teaches. In Babel, people bring their consciences into a mere **historical narrative** <note>original: "History"; referring to a literal or intellectual-only understanding of scripture</note> and flatter them in a **courtly manner** with Christ’s suffering and death; there, they teach the forgiveness of sins only as a **historical event**.

3. They treat it like a worldly court <note>original: "Judicatory"</note>, where someone's faults are pardoned out of *mercy* <note>original: "Grace"</note> even though the person remains clearly wicked in their heart.

4. It is completely different here: God will have no *deceitful* hypocrites. He does not take sin away from us in *such* a manner—where we cling to the knowledge and comfort ourselves with the suffering of Christ, and yet, in our conscience, we *dwell* in abominations.

<margin>* John 3:3, 5, 7</margin>
5. It is said, * *You must be born again <note>original: "a New"</note>, or else you shall not see the kingdom of God.*

6. Anyone who flatters <note>original: "tickle"</note> themselves with Christ’s suffering and death and claims it for their own—yet remains willfully unregenerated in the **nature of Adam** <note>original: "Adamical Man"</note>—is like a person who comforts themselves with the idea that their Lord will give them land. They fail to consider that they are *not* the Lord's son, and the Lord has promised to give the land only to his son. It is the same in this case.

7. If you wish to possess the land of your Lord and have it as your own, then you must become his rightful and **true son**.
<margin>* Genesis 21:10; Galatians 4:3</margin>
* *For the son of the bondwoman shall not inherit with the free son.* The son of the mere **historical narrative** <note>original: "History"</note> is a stranger.

8. You must be born or generated by God in Christ so that you may be a <gloss>† Or a son begotten or generated of his own body.</gloss> **true, literal son** <note>original: "bodily Sonne"</note>. Then you are God’s child and an heir to the suffering and death of Christ.

9. And Christ’s death is your death; his resurrection from the grave is...

<summary>The author argues that salvation requires a genuine spiritual rebirth rather than a mere intellectual acceptance of the "history" of Christ's death. He criticizes institutional religious teaching (Babel) for offering a false sense of forgiveness to those who remain unchanged in heart.</summary>

<keywords>regeneration, Babel, new birth, Adamical Man, forgiveness of sins, spiritual sonship, historical faith</keywords>

...is your resurrection; his ascension into heaven is your ascension into heaven; and the kingdom of his eternal life is your kingdom.

<margin>* Note.</margin>
10. In that you are his true and rightful son, born of his flesh and blood, you are * an heir of all his goods; otherwise, you cannot be Christ’s child and heir.

11. So long as the earthly kingdom sticks to you—within your image—you are the earthly son of the fallen Adam. No flattering hypocrisy will help; you can speak as many good words before God as you want, but you remain a stranger’s child.

<margin>† Luke 15:20</margin>
12. And God’s goods do not belong to you until you return to the Father with † the lost son <note>original: "lost sonne"; a reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son from the Gospel of Luke.</note>, carrying a true sorrow and repentance for your lost inheritance.

13. You must go out with your **willing-spirit** <term>The inner drive or volition of a person, directed toward a specific purpose or desire.</term> from the earthly life, and break or destroy your earthly **willing** <note>original: "willing"; here meaning the act of directing one's will toward worldly desires</note>. This is painful to the mind and the willing-spirit, to forsake the treasure it once possessed (in which that spirit was formed), but you must enter into God's willing.

### 14. And there you sow your seed

in God’s kingdom; and you are born again in God, like fruit that grows in God’s field. For your will receives God's power—Christ's body—and the new body in God grows within you.

15. And then you are God’s child, and Christ’s goods belong to you. His merits are your merits; his suffering, death, and resurrection are all yours. You are a member of his body, and his spirit is your spirit. * He leads you on right paths; and everything you do, you do for God.
<margin>* Proverbs 4:11</margin>

16. You sow in this world and reap in the heaven of God. You are God’s "work of wonder" and reveal his wonders in the earthly life, drawing yourself with your willing-spirit into the

### Holy Mystery.

17. Notice this, you who are covetous, proud, envious, false judges, and wickedly malicious: you who direct your will and desire into earthly goods, into money and abundance, and into the pleasure and luxury of this life. You consider money and goods to be your treasure and set your desire within them, and yet, despite all that, you still *want* to be called God’s children.

18. You stand and act like hypocrites <note>original: "dissemble"</note> before God; you ask him to forgive your sins, but you remain with your old nature <note>original: "Image"</note> in **Adam’s skin** and **Adam’s flesh** <note>Metaphors for the fallen, sinful human state inherited from Adam.</note>. You **comfort** yourselves with the sufferings of Christ, but you are **only** pretenders; you are **not** God’s children.

### Chapter 8: How a Person Becomes the Child of God, Part 3

19. You must be born in God if you wish to be his children, otherwise you deceive yourselves along with the hypocrites or pretenders who present a glittering facade <note>original: "Glistring Colour"; a deceptive or superficial outward appearance.</note> before you.

20. They teach, and are \* not known by God, nor are they † sent to teach; they do it for their own bellies and for the sake of worldly honor. They are \* the Great Whore at **Babel** <term>In this context, "Babel" refers to spiritual confusion and the corrupt, institutionalized church systems that the author critiques.</term>, who flatter God with their lips, but with their heart and willing-spirit they serve the † dragon at **Babel**.

† Jeremiah 14:14; 23:21; and 27:15.
\* Revelation 17:1.
† Revelation 12:3.
</margin>

21. Beloved Mind, if you wish to be the child of God, then prepare yourself for attacks and for tribulation. It is no easy or gentle entrance into the child’s life, especially where reason lies captive in the earthly kingdom.

<margin>
How the child of God must prepare for attacks and tribulation, etc.
</margin>

22. Reason must be broken, and the will must depart from reason; it must sow itself into God’s kingdom in lowly obedience, just as a grain of seed is sown in a field or soil. Within reason, it must make itself as if it were dead and surrender itself to God, and so the new fruit grows in God’s kingdom.

23. Thus, that person stands in a threefold life <note>A core concept in the author's theology, referring to the three "principles" or realms: the dark world of fire, the light world of God’s majesty, and the outer world of the four elements.</note>, and all of it belongs to God.

24. The inward fiery essences of the first principle <term>The "First Principle" represents the fiery foundation of nature and the soul, which must be transformed by the light of Christ.</term> become incorporated with the new body in Christ, so that they flow up into Christ’s flesh and blood out of God's will; and their fire is God’s fire, out of which **love, meekness, and humility burn.**

25. Where the Holy Spirit goes forth and helps him to endure the battle against earthly reason, as well as against the perished, corrupt flesh and the will of the devil, \* his yoke of earthly willing becomes lighter for him; but in this world, he must remain in the struggle.

<margin>
\* Matthew 11:30.
Provision for the outward life.
</margin>

26. For the earthly life requires sustenance, which he must seek, and yet he ought not to fix his will and heart upon it.

27. He must trust God, yet his **earthly reason always lapses into doubting**; it will fail him. It will always want to see God, and yet it cannot, for God does not dwell in the earthly kingdom, but in himself.

28. Thus, because reason cannot see God, it must be forced into hope.

29. In that state, Doubting runs counter to Faith or Believing and seeks to destroy *Hope*. Therefore, the earnest will, along with the true spiritual image, must strive and fight against earthly reason. This causes distress, and things often go sadly.

30. This is especially true if Reason focuses on the *course* of this world, and if the will-spirit—behaving as if it were foolish—has *respect* for the ways of this world. In such times, it is said: *be sober, watch closely, and pray*. This means that you must *tame* your earthly reason and make it as if it were dead, so that God’s Spirit may find a place within you.

<margin>* Romans 8:28.</margin>

of a new little branch out of the *Tree of Faith*.

<meta>This page provides a bibliographic catalog of the works of the German mystic Jakob Böhme (here spelled "Jacob Behme") available in English as of 1659. It serves as an advertisement and finding aid for followers of his "Theosophic" philosophy.</meta>

# A Catalog of Jakob Böhme’s Books,
->Printed in *English*<-
### According to the numbering in the catalog found at the end of the book *The Forty Questions*, printed in 1647.

1. The *Aurora* <note>original: "The Day-Spring" or "Dawn"; Böhme's first major work.</note>.
2. The Three Principles of the Divine Essence or Substance.
3. The Threefold Life of Man.
4. The Forty Questions of the Soul.
5. The Incarnation of Jesus Christ.
8. Concerning the Last Times, or the 1,000-year Sabbath; these are his fourth and fifth epistles.
9. The *Signature of All Things* <note>One of Böhme's most famous works, arguing that every object in nature reveals its inner spiritual character through its outer form.</note>.
10. Concerning the Four Complexions <note>The four temperaments: choleric, melancholic, sanguine, and phlegmatic.</note>, written to comfort a soul in temptation.
12. Reflections on Esaias Stiefel’s Book.
13. Concerning True Repentance.
14. Concerning True Resignation.
15. Concerning Regeneration.
<note>Items 13, 14, and 15 are grouped together as:</note>
} These together are known as *The Way to Christ*.
16. Concerning Predestination and Election; along with
17. An Appendix regarding Repentance.
18. The *Mysterium Magnum* <note>original: "The Great Mystery"</note>, an exposition of Genesis. This work concerns the manifestation or revelation of the Divine Word through the three principles of the divine essence. It also covers the origin of the world and creation, explaining the kingdoms of nature and grace for a better understanding of the Old and New Testaments, and the nature of Adam and Christ.
19. A Table of the Three Principles, explained.
20. Concerning the Supersensual Life <note>A dialogue about spiritual life that exists beyond the physical senses.</note>.
22. Concerning the Two Testaments of Christ, namely: Baptism and the Lord's Supper.
23. A Dialogue between the enlightened and unenlightened soul regarding illumination.

<column-break/>

25. The 177 Theosophical Questions, without the thirteen answers <note>Böhme intended to answer all 177 questions, but only completed a portion of them.</note>.
26. An Epitome or abstract of the *Mysterium Magnum*.
28. An exposition of the Threefold World.
31. Consisting of thirty-five letters or epistles from Jakob Böhme to several of his friends concerning the Divine Mysteries.

A *Clavis* <note>original: "Key"</note> or key to his writings. Prophecies of the end of the world, collected from several of Jakob Böhme’s writings, titled *Mercurius Teutonicus* <note>original: "The German Messenger"</note>.

---

The Life of Jakob Böhme, written by Durand Hotham, Esq.

---

Philosophy reformed and improved, containing three books by Paracelsus <note>A famous Swiss physician and alchemist who influenced Böhme.</note> addressed to the Athenians; these are helpful for understanding Jakob Böhme’s writings.
Also, these philosophical pieces:
*Magia Adamica* <note>original: "Adamic Magic"</note>, or the antiquity of magic; concerning the magician's "Heavenly Chaos" and the first matter of all things.
*Lumen de Lumine* <note>original: "Light from Light"</note>, or a new magical light discovered to the world.
The Chemist’s Key to shut and open the true doctrine of corruption and generation, illustrated by the true light of nature.

---

->These books are sold by Lodowick Lloyd, near the Castle in Cornhill, London, 1659.<-

Man is his own God or Devil — 43.

The Holy Spirit does not use the wicked — 110.

Faith free from inclination — 199.

One spirit with God — 203.

Evil arises from the eternal substance, but not from God — 205. <note>original: "et subs"; likely "eternal substance" or the Latin "eternal substantia." Böhme argued that the potential for evil exists in the structural nature of the universe, but God is not its source.</note>

Similitudes — 205. <note>Parables or spiritual analogies.</note>

Nature comes not from the Willing itself, but from the longing of the willing — 205.

That which imagines into the seeking is one life in Nature; that which imagines into the free willing of God is one spirit with God — 205-206. <note>Böhme uses "imagination" to describe the formative power of the will to shape its own reality.</note>

God is free in regard to Nature — 206.

Soul and spirit — 207.

Original sin is traced to one seed — 208.

Man’s Law and Nature’s Law — 228.
